Announcements
Better Gut, Better Sleep? Gut-Brain Study | Earn up to HKD 500 「腸」通無阻，瞓得更好？「腸·腦」研究 | 最高可獲 HKD 500 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Jephthah Cheung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
lokcheung@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
近年醫學界發現，我們的腸道健康與大腦息息相關！原來「便秘」和「睡眠質素」的改變，可能是腦部退化的早期信號。為了深入了解這條神奇的「腸腦連線」，香港中文大學精神科學系睡眠研究組現正招募研究參加者。
研究對象:
年齡介乎 50 至 80 歲
關注腸道健康或者受便秘問題困擾（如排便困難、次數較少等）
沒有腦退化、精神疾病史
參加者需完成以下簡單程序：
填寫問卷 及 進行簡單面談
進行一次非入侵性睡眠檢測
記錄連續兩星期「大便日記」
進行一次結腸運輸試驗
收集一次大便樣本
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者最多可獲 HKD 500 超市禮券的津貼
如對本研究有興趣，請透過以下連結報名參加：
[網址連結:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eeTcY6hrKILNwhg
]
如對研究內容有任何疑問，歡迎致電 3919 7792 / 9568 9006 或 WhatsApp 9568 9006與負責研究人員聯絡、查詢詳情。謝謝
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Recent research suggests that gut health is closely linked to brain function. Changes in bowel habits (e.g. constipation) and sleep quality may even be early signs of neurodegeneration.
To better understand this “gut–brain axis, we sincerely invite you to take part in our research study.
Who can join:
Aged 50–80
Concerned about gut health or bothered by constipation
No history of dementia or psychiatric disorders
What you will do:
Complete questionnaires and a brief interview
Undergo a sleep assessment
Record a 2-week bowel diary
Complete a colonic transit time test
Collect one stool sample
Incentive:
All assessments are free of charge.
Eligible participants may receive up to HKD 500 in supermarket vouchers upon completion.
Interested? Please sign up here:
[
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eeTcY6hrKILNwhg
]
Enquiries:
3919 7792 / 9568 9006
WhatsApp 9568 9006

For enquiries, please write to:

bodyText:

»
2026/07/24
»
Announcements
⏰ Term‑End Reminder: Blackboard Course and Panopto Access for Students  - ITSC
From: eLearning Team, ITSC
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
elearning@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
While arrangements may vary, students should assume that Blackboard courses will no longer be accessible after the end of the term unless otherwise advised. For details, please refer to:
Access to Blackboard Courses and Panopto Videos
ITSC Website: Learning Management System (LMS) – Blackboard
For graduating students:
Blackboard and its integrated services (such as Panopto, Gradescope, and FeedbackFruits) are NOT available to alumni. Please download and back up all materials, if possible, before the end of the term and/or before your account expires, as needed.
Please also refer to the
Checklist for Graduate-to-be
.
For other students:
You are advised to download and back up all materials before term-end, where applicable.
Student access to Blackboard courses will be discontinued from the fourth year onward. Students may access course materials from the current academic year and the two preceding years, subject to the decision of the instructor or TA/support staff.
For questions, please contact us at:
elearning@cuhk.edu.hk
or ITSC Service Desk (
https://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
).

For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

title: Student helper needed!! Priority given to education/science faculty 招募學生助理【教育及科學學院優先】
bodyText:

2026/07/24
»
Announcements
Student helper needed!! Priority given to education/science faculty  招募學生助理【教育及科學學院優先】 - Sports Science and Physical Education
From: Daisy Wan
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
kakeiwan@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
一項有關熱壓力（Heat Stress）對學生影響的研究即將展開！我們現正招募學生助理（Student Helpers），歡迎有興趣累積研究經驗，或親身了解真實教育環境運作的同學參與。
研究資料收集日期：
2026年9月至11月（實際日期將於8月中公佈）
工作時間：
日間時段
工作地點：
沙田區、港島西區、中大校園
優先招募對象：
教育學院、理學院本科生
酬金：
按大學學生助理標準時薪計算，並有機會提供交通津貼
報名方法：
如有興趣參與，請先填寫以下表格，並於表格內填寫有興趣擔任的崗位及已知可工作的日期和時間。研究團隊將於2026年8月中聯絡合適申請者，提供進一步資料及工作安排。
https://forms.cloud.microsoft/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=gTdBhKa7s0W74E8XxpDaapWiNw_U0n9Mpg9NAqiXCahUQ0cxQlhVWkI4UlhaOFNQQTRCSE01RTY3My4u&route=shorturl
查詢：
如有任何疑問，歡迎聯絡 Daisy（電話：3943 8069 - 可WhatsApp），或電郵至
kakeiwan@cuhk.edu.hk
。
期待你的參與！
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A data collection regarding a heat stress study is on the way! We would like to recruit student helpers (ST) who would like to gain research experience or have first-hand insights into real-world educational settings. Below are the details:
Date: September - November 2026 (exact date TBC in mid-August)
Time: Day-time
Location: Shatin District, Western District, CUHK campus
Priority ST group: Undergraduates from the Faculty of Education/ Science
Compensation: Standard student helper hourly rate + possible transportation subsidy
If you are interested, please first fill in the form below to indicate the position you are interested in and the known availability. You will be conatcted in mid August for futher details. Should you have any questions or concern, please feel free to contact Daisy (3943 8069 - WhatsApp available) or email to kakeiwan@cuhk.edu.hk
Sign-up Form:
https://forms.cloud.microsoft/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=gTdBhKa7s0W74E8XxpDaapWiNw_U0n9Mpg9NAqiXCahUQ0cxQlhVWkI4UlhaOFNQQTRCSE01RTY3My4u&route=shorturl
We look forward to seeing you!

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

From: CUHK RAISe+ Team

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
As we anticipate the Government will call for applications for the 4th Solicitation Exercise of the RAISe+ Scheme around September 2026, we are calling for the internal registration among CUHK now. If you are interested in it, please complete the
Online Registration Form
by
31 Aug 2026 (Mon)
.
We would like to invite you to attend a briefing session on 4 Aug 2026 (Tue). We believe you will gain more insight and have a deeper understanding of the RAISe+ application after attending the briefing session, which will help you to better prepare your application for both CUHK internal registration and ITC application.
RAISe+ 4th Cohort Briefing Session
Date: 4 Aug 2026 (Tue)
Time: 09:30 am - 11:30 am
Venue: Room UGA, UG/F, InnoPort, CUHK
Registration Link: https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13737242
Here is the latest
RAISe+ funding guideline of the last cohort
for your reference. For more details on RAISe+ Scheme, please visit
RAISe+ Scheme
on KTO’s website. A briefing session would be held in early August, details will be announced later.
About RAISe+ Scheme
The Research, Academic and Industry Sectors One-plus (RAISe+) Scheme aims to help the prospective research teams with good potential to transform, realise and commercialise the research and development (“R&D”) outcomes and become successful start-ups within around five years. For more details, please refer to
ITC website
.

Announcements
[Free of charge] [An allowance of up to HKD $1,000 will be provided upon successful enrollment] Recruitment of Diabetes Patients (Aged 18-70 years) for clinical trials of Chinese Medicine (Powder) Treatment [費用全免] [成功參與者可獲得高達港幣 $1,000 的津貼] 招募年齡介於 18-70 歲的糖尿病人士- 中藥(沖劑)治療臨床研究 - Department of Medicine and Therapeutics
From: Maggie Lee
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
maggielee@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
[
新中藥方劑治療
2
型糖尿病的臨床安全性、有效性和多組評價：對
β
細胞功能和胰島素抵抗的影響】
香港中文大學內科及藥物治療學系與香港中文大學香港中西醫結合醫學研究所現正聯合進行一項為期36週，以內服中藥(沖劑)治療 2 型糖尿病人
 研究對象：18至70歲華人
沒有重大疾病，沒有服用中藥， 身體質量指數 (BMI) ≥18 kg/m²  (公斤 ÷ 米 ÷ 米)
不吸煙或已戒煙至少 12 個月，如女性目前未懷孕
患糖尿病未滿 6 年，且在過去 3 個月內未使用任何降血糖藥物（包括胰島素）治療
至少具備以下其中一項風險因素:
糖尿病家族史 (尤其父母或兄弟姐妹在40歲前診斷 )
代謝綜合症 (3高：高血糖，高血壓，高膽固醇)
超重或肥胖
脂肪肝
多囊卵巢綜合症
妊娠糖尿病病史
如不確定自己是否患有糖尿病，會安排你服用葡萄糖飲料（75 克口服葡萄糖耐量試驗）
研究內容：中西醫評估、心電圖、肝纖維化掃描、抽血檢查、填寫問卷、服用研究中藥或安慰劑等
地點：新界沙田威爾斯醫院，舊座，3 樓，3M 病房 - 糖尿及內分泌研究中心
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者可獲得高達港幣 $1,000 的津貼，名額有限，先到先得！
閣下如對本研究有興趣請透過以下連結報名參加：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=3542692
如果初步合適參與研究，負責同事將稍後聯絡你，謝謝
如對研究內容有任何疑問，歡迎致電  3505 3897 / 6937 3365 或 WhatsApp 6937 3365與負責研究人員聯絡、查詢詳情。
[Clinical safety, efficacy and multiomic evaluation of a novel Chinese Medicine formula in Type 2 diabetes: Effects on beta-cell function and insulin resistance
.]
Department of Medicine and Therapeutics and Hong Kong Institute of Integrative Medicine, CUHK are jointly conducting a 36-week clinical study on the use of oral traditional Chinese medicine (granule form) for treating type 2 diabetes.
Eligibility Criteria: Ethnic Chinese individuals aged 18 to 70 years
No major illnesses, not currently taking any traditional Chinese medicine, and with a Body Mass Index (BMI) ≥ 18 kg/m² (kg ÷ metre ÷ metre)
Non-smokers or those who have quit smoking for at least 12 months; females must not be currently pregnant
Diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for less than 6 years and have not used any glucose-lowering medications (including insulin) in the past 3 months
Must have at least one of the following risk factors:
Family history of diabetes (especially if parents or siblings were diagnosed before age of 40)
Metabolic syndrome (three highs: high blood sugar, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol)
Overweight or obesity
Fatty liver
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
History of gestational diabetes
If you are unsure whether you have diabetes, a 75g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) will be arranged for you.

Study Procedures Include:
Chinese and Western medical assessments, Electrocardiogram (ECG), Liver fibrosis scan, Blood tests, Questionnaire completion, Taking either the study Chinese medicine or a placebo
Location: Ward 3M, 3/F, Old Block, Diabetes and Endocrinology Research Centre, Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin, New Territories
Free of charge to participate.
Successful participants may receive an allowance of up to HKD $1,000.
Limited quota – first come, first served!
Register via the following link:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=3542692
If you are eligible based on initial assessment, our research team will contact you shortly. Thank you!
For inquiries, please contact:
3505 3897 / 6937 3365
WhatsApp: 6937 3365

For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

招募參與者：社交焦慮短期介入訓練計劃
六週指導式自助練習，處理社會評價與自我批評
打破自我批評的惡性循環
找回自我肯定的正向情緒

香港中文大學校園內，全程免費
香港中文大學臨床心理科學實驗室團隊現正推行一項針對社交焦慮問題的短期介入訓練計劃，誠邀符合資格的人士參與。
社交焦慮不止影響我們如何應對社交場合，亦關乎我們如何看待自己，以及如何與他人建立聯繫。目前，社交焦慮問題的治療多採用認知行為取向，研究證實能有效改善個人在社交情境中的功能表現。本計劃則是團隊基於實證研究開發的新訓練方案，採用社會情緒取向，聚焦於處理個人與自我及他人的關係。本項目遵循階梯式照護模式 (stepped-care model)，定位為指導式自助 (guided self-help) 短期介入方案，旨在以較少的時間投入及心理負擔，為參加者提供有效支援。
訓練為期6週，包括「每週1次實體會面 + 自助練習 + 線上心理評估訪談及問卷」 ； 訓練完成後1個月和六個月進行隨訪評估
 「招募要求」
年滿18歲或以上；廣東話流利；
在社交焦慮方面感到困擾，例如在社交或公開場合強烈緊張焦慮、擔心自己被負面評價、迴避社交場合，並明顯影響工作或學習；
現時並未接受其他形式的心理治療或精神科藥物治療；
能夠親身前往香港中文大學校園參與訓練。

「參與流程」
報名後，我們將聯絡您安排篩選問卷及訪談，以確認是否適合參加本計劃，並邀請符合條件者參與訓練。

「報名連結」
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eDNm9u2HOUkR302
如有疑問，歡迎聯絡研究團隊：cdclabcuhk@gmail.com
本計劃已獲香港中文大學–新界東醫院聯網臨床研究倫理聯席委員會審批（CUHK-NTEC CREC 2025.796）。
所有個人資料僅用作研究篩選及介入用途，並會嚴格保密。
香港中文大學臨床心理科學實驗室團隊
Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory
Recruiting Participants: Brief Psychological Training Programme for Social Anxiety
The Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently conducting a brief intervention programme for individuals experiencing social anxiety difficulties. We invite eligible individuals to participate.
Social anxiety not only affects how we cope in social situations but also involves how we view ourselves and relate to others. While cognitive-behavioural approaches are widely used and evidence-based for treating social anxiety, our team has developed a novel training protocol grounded in empirical research that adopts a social-emotional approach, focusing on improving individuals’ relationships with themselves and with others. Following the stepped-care model, this programme is designed as a brief guided self-help intervention, aiming to provide effective support with minimal time commitment and psychological burden.
The training programme spans 6 weeks and includes:
Weekly in-person sessions (once per week)
Self-help practice exercises
Questionnaire assessments
Follow-up evaluations will be conducted one month and six months after the training.
「Eligibility Criteria」
Aged 18 or above
Fluent in Cantonese
Experiencing significant social anxiety-related distress (e.g., intense anxiety in social or public settings, fear of negative evaluation, avoidance of social situations, with noticeable impact on work or study)
Not currently receiving other forms of psychological therapy or psychiatric medication
Able to attend in-person sessions on the CUHK campus
「Procedures」
After registration, we will contact you to arrange a screening questionnaire and an interview to determine your suitability for the programme. Eligible participants will then be invited to join the training.
「Registration Link」
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eDNm9u2HOUkR302
For enquiries, please contact our research team at: cdclabcuhk@gmail.com
This study has been approved by the Joint CUHK-NTEC Clinical Research Ethics Committee (CUHK-NTEC CREC 2025.796).
All personal data collected will be used solely for research screening and intervention purposes and will be kept strictly confidential.

  [Online experiment] Looking for native English speakers
Prof. Haerim Hwang (Department of English, CUHK) is looking for participants for a study on language production.
Which participants are we looking for?
- English is your first/native and dominant language
- Your graduate degree is not in the field of linguistics
- Can use your laptop/computer and have access to stable internet (no smartphones, laptops, or hotspot)
- Can participate in an experiment on Zoom in a quiet environment
- Have Chrome on your laptop/computer
How do I participate?
1. Fill out this questionnaire
-- English speakers: https://forms.gle/ttuhGGCwRx2n95kBA
2. Our research team will reach out to you, confirming your availability.
3. It will take approximately 2 hours to complete these tasks.
What do I get out of the study?
You will get HK$250 in cash upon the completion of the task.
Your participation will enhance our understanding of how people process English sentences.
Questions?
Contact Prof. Haerim Hwang at haerimhwang@cuhk.edu.hk
Ethics Approval
The Chinese University of Hong Kong Survey and Behavioural Research Ethics Committee SBREC (fssc02@cuhk.edu.hk) has vetted the study (Approval ID: SBRE-22-0026D). If you have any concerns regarding ethics, please contact them.

Announcements
Microsoft Copilot Chat Tips Compare Documents: Spot Differences & Key Changes  - ITSC
From: ITSC
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
itsc@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Ever needed to compare two versions of a document and dreaded the tedious side-by-side reading? Upload
both versions
into
M365 Copilot
and let it do the detective work! It will highlight differences, additions, and removals in seconds.
Try this prompt — copy & paste it!
"I've uploaded two versions of our handbook — the current version and the proposed update. Please: (1) List all sections that were changed, added, or removed, (2) For each change, summarize what was modified and why it might matter, (3) Highlight any changes  (4) Create a change log table with columns: Section, Type of Change, Summary, Impact Level (High/Medium/Low)."
Why this works:
Structuring the comparison as a change log with impact levels turns a tedious manual comparison into an instant, prioritized review. Decision-makers can focus on high-impact changes first!

Use for
: Contract revisions, policy updates, proposal iterations, budget comparisons (upload two Excel files!), or any before/after document review. Saves
hours
of side-by-side reading!

for even more helpful guidance and best practices.

What are the essential soft skills in the workplace? Co-op@CUHK helps you meet employers’ expectations!   - Office of Co-operative Education Programme (OCEP)
From: Office of Co-operative Education Programme (OCEP)
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
coop@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

What are the essential soft skills in the workplace?
Co-op@CUHK helps you meet employers’ expectations!

Have you ever wondered what qualities employers value most? Employers are seeking more than just good grades. Strong soft skills, such as analytical thinking, resilience, flexibility, agility, leadership, and social influence, are essential for success in the workplace. Co-op’s dedicated courses help you develop these important competencies with our preparatory courses.
COOP3001: Unlocking Employability Potential and Personal Branding (1 Unit)
With sessions on understanding oneself through Personality Dimensions, mastering first impressions, career planning and related topics, Co-op students will be able to:
Demonstrate a deeper understanding of their personality, strengths and interests, enabling them to build a distinctive personal brand (
Self-awareness
)
Identify their career aspirations and analyse labour market opportunities to make informed career development plans (
Analytical Thinking
).
Adapt pragmatic strategies to changing workplace expectations (
Flexibility and Agility
).
COOP3002: Developing Workplace Professionalism (2 Units)
Through classes on Excel skills, problem solving in the era of AI, professional email writing, workplace etiquette and together with other experiential learning initiatives such as Outward Bound Training, Co-op students will be able to:
Apply analytical or AI tools effectively to support workplace productivity and decision-making (
Technological Literacy
).
Analyse workplace challenges critically, as well as develop pragmatic and innovative recommendations (
Creative Thinking
)
Communicate professionally through written correspondence and workplace interactions (
Empathy and Active Listening
)
Co-op provides a valuable platform for students to cultivate essential soft skills and better prepare themselves for the challenges at workplace. Application for the 6th cohort is now open! Fill out the
online application form
and join us!

.

Dear students, the research team from the CUHK School of Public Health and Primary Care cordially invites you to participate in a survey on the well-being and mental health of local post-secondary students.
Spend
15-20 minutes
sharing your happiness and stress, and receive a
HK$100 voucher
(PARKnSHOP / Wellcome / Starbucks / Apple Store) upon completion! No fancy words needed—just your honest feelings.

HK permanent resident aged 18-24
Local full-time undergraduate (Degree) or sub-degree (Associate / Higher Diploma) student
Able to read and understand Traditional Chinese or English
Able to complete the online survey using a smartphone, tablet, or computer

Data is strictly confidential, participation is entirely voluntary, and you can withdraw at any time.

From: Queenie Chow
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
literacy@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
誠邀閣下與子女參與一項關於華語兒童中英數能力的跨學科大型研究，詳情如下：
對象：
幼稚園高班至六年級單生兒和雙胞胎學生（包括同卵雙生和異卵雙生）
學童家長
學童需以廣東話為母語，並在香港居住 2.5 年以上
目的：
建立學童在中、英文讀寫和數學能力發展的多模態模型，以及設計能夠全面反映兒童在這三方面表現的網上測試工具
研究內容：
第一部分
學童：中英文和數學能力的測試
，分成網上測試和面對面測試兩部分。網上測試分為六個區域，各需時約40分鐘。網上測試毋須一次完成，參加者可自行安排時間分段執行，在四星期內完成所有項目即可。
面對面測試在網上測試完成後另約時間進行，約需45分鐘
家長：
在網上測試平台接受
約
15分鐘的語文及數學測試
，及填寫關於學童學習情況與家庭語言環境的
問卷
第二部分（可選擇是否參與）
學童：腦電圖測試（EEG），約2小時
報酬：每年測試完結後將收到：
(1) 測試結果的個人報告；(2) 港幣200元超級市場現金券；(3) 小禮物，
參與腦電圖 (EEG) 部份的學生另有250元超級市場現金券
研究詳情及報名請見以下網頁：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4OWk4Rmnmb0M20e
如對是項研究有任何疑問或查詢，歡迎聯絡本項目的首席研究員Urs Maurer教授（電郵: umaurer@cuhk.edu.hk）或研究小組（電話：3943-4379；電郵：
lifespandevlab.cuhk@gmail.com
）。
We are recruiting for a multi-disciplinary study about the Chinese, English, and Mathematical abilities among Chinese-speaking children in Hong Kong. Details are as below:
Target participants:
Singletons and twins (both identical and fraternal) from K3 to P6 in the 2024/25 school year
Students’ parents
The child participant must be a native Cantonese speaker and have lived in Hong Kong for more than 2.5 years.
Content:
Part 1
Students
: A series of assessments on Chinese, English, and mathematics on the project’s online testing platform. The tasks are divided into six portions; each takes about 40 minutes to finish. Online testing can be completed at your own pace, as long as all tasks are completed within 4 weeks.
A follow-up face-to-face session (45 minutes) will be arranged upon completion of the online testing.
Parents
: Short online testing on language and mathematics abilities (15 minutes), as well as a set of questionnaires on children’s learning and home language environment
Part 2 (optional)
Students: electroencephalography (EEG) test (~2 hour)
Rewards: After each round of testing, participants will receive:
(1) Personal performance report; (2) $200 supermarket vouchers; (3) a gift (for students); EEG participants will receive an additional $250 worth of supermarket vouchers
The details of the study and the registration form can be found in the following link:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4OWk4Rmnmb0M20e
Should you have any enquiries, please contact Prof. Urs Maurer, the principle investigator (umaurer@cuhk.edu.hk) or the research team (3943-4379 or lifespandevlab.cuhk@gmail.com).
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

Requirements for participants:
1) Fluent in English,
2) Have no prior experience with any sign language,
3) Be available to attend on two CONSECUTIVE days.
The study will take place in the Esther Lee Building, Room 407. There are two sessions: the first takes around 40 minutes and the second 30 minutes, held on consecutive days. You will receive HKD 90 as compensation, paid immediately after you complete the second session.

bodyText:

2026/07/17
»
Announcements
Recruitment of 【Native Cantonese-speaking】Participants ⭐(250HKD)⭐ in a Psychology Experiment about Chinese Two-character Words 誠邀【母語粵語者】參與關於中文複合詞的心理學研究（250HKD） - Department of Education Psychology
From: Xi Cheng
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
xicheng3@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
***Please Note that this study requires reading Chinese words, so we would like to invite students who are native Cantonese speakers to participate.***
教育心理學系謝志成教授一項關於中文複合詞的研究誠意邀請與會者參與。
對象：
**參加者需為粵語是母語的本港學生；
**參與者需要有良好的視力或矯正視力；
**參與者需慣性用右手。
**參與者年齡需大於18嵗。
研究內容：整個實驗將為期三節（每節之間間隔不超過一星期）進行，每節需要 1 至 1.5 小時，完成3節後可得到250港元作為現金補償。
地點：陳國本樓707E室
參與方式：如有興趣，請點此連結報名https://forms.gle/znR7QB79PVof2F87A
（報名時個人資料包括：姓名、學號、性別、年齡、學系、年級、聯絡電話、聯絡電郵。）
有興趣的同學請提供每週至少兩個時間段，以便安排。
*若閣下沒有收到我們的電郵，代表所選的時間已額滿，多謝！
*若已參加過【對於中文複合詞所表達的情感】的研究，請勿重複報名。
如果對實驗有任何疑問，歡迎聯絡
xicheng3@cuhk.edu.hk
。

bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/07/17
»
Announcements
Study on Public Perceptions of Disease Burden in HK [招募30-69歲男士, 50-69歲女士] 香港市民對疾病負擔的研究調查 ($50現金報酬) - JCSPHPC
From: Zoe Tam
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
zoetam@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學醫學院 賽馬會公共衞生及基層醫療學院 正進行一項研究，探討香港市民對於不同疾病造成的負擔的看法。
參加者資格
30-69歲男士，或50-69歲⼥⼠
香港居⺠
能閱讀或理解中文
參加方式
問卷調查（電話訪問，或者自行於網上作答），過程需時約20-30分鐘。
答謝安排
完成問卷並經核實後，合資格的受訪者可透過電子支付方式，即PayMe、FPS轉數快或支付寶(香港)，獲港幣50元以作答謝。名額有限，額滿即止。
參加方法（一）、自行填寫網上問卷：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_cvVnx4h5B1qTiEm
參加方法（二）、接受電話訪問：
請聯絡研究團隊。
聲明
本研究自2026年5月8日 開始招募參加者。若您曾經參與此問卷調查，
重覆作答將被視為無效
。若您對參加資格存疑，歡迎聯絡研究團隊。
查詢
本研究已獲香港中文大學 – 新界東醫院聯網臨床研究倫理聯席委員會審查和批准。如有任何查詢，歡迎聯絡研究團隊。
聯絡方式
電話: 2252 8793 (談小姐)
WhatsApp: 6752 1018
電郵: zoetam@cuhk.edu.hk
The Jockey Club School of Public Health and Primary Care, Faculty of Medicine, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, is conducting a research study to explore how Hong Kong residents perceive the burden caused by different diseases.
Eligibility Criteria
Male aged 30 to 69, or Female aged 50 to 69
Hong Kong residents
Able to read or understand Chinese
How to Participate
Participants will be asked to complete an
questionnaire online or via telephone
, which will take approximately
20-30 minutes
to complete.
Appreciation
Upon completion of the questionnaire, the eligibile participants will receive
HK$50
as a token of appreciation via
electronic payment
(PayMe, FPS, or AlipayHK). Quotas are limited and recruitment will close once all places are filled.
Participation Method (1): Self-administration of the Online Survey
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_cvVnx4h5B1qTiEm
Participation Method (2): Telephone Interview
Please contact the research team.
Disclaimer
Subject reruitment for this study began on 8 May 2026. If you have previously participated in this survey, repeated participation will not be considered valid. If you are unsure about your eligibility, please contact the research team.
Enquiries
This study has been reviewed and approved by the Joint Chinese University of Hong Kong – New Territories East Cluster Clinical Research Ethics Committee. For enquiries, please contact the research team.
Contact Information
Telephone: 2252 8793 (Ms. Zoe TAM)
WhatsApp: 6752 1018
E-mail address: zoetam@cuhk.edu.hk

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

title: HK$400 Stipend and a Chiikawa gift; Traditional Chinese Character Reading/Writing Experiment for Fourth-Grade Students in Hong Kong 400港币酬劳和吉伊卡哇 (Chiikawa) 精美禮品；香港小學四年級學生繁體字讀寫能力測試
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/07/17
»
Announcements
HK$400 Stipend and a Chiikawa gift; Traditional Chinese Character Reading/Writing Experiment for Fourth-Grade Students in Hong Kong  400港币酬劳和吉伊卡哇 (Chiikawa) 精美禮品；香港小學四年級學生繁體字讀寫能力測試 - Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
From: Xiaohui RAO
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155197282@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
你了解孩子的漢字（繁體字）讀寫能力嗎？不要錯過這次有趣又有意義的研究機會！輕鬆參與測試，不但可以獲得報酬，還有精美禮品帶回家！
測試內容：
我們現邀小學四年級學生（剛讀完四年級，準備開始五年級）來完成
繁體字
書寫及閱讀任務。我們會使用專業設備記錄書寫軌跡與力度，並透過語言小遊戲評估閱讀與語言能力。
測試時間
：約兩小時
測試地點：
香港中文大學梁銶琚樓（語言學系）。
參與回報：
完成測試可獲
HKD 400
現金
，另加精美「吉伊卡哇（Chiikawa）」文具禮品
参与者需要符合以下要求：
1 小學四年級學生（剛讀完四年級，準備開始五年級）
2 學校以
繁體字
及
廣東話
教授中文課程
3 視力正常（可佩戴眼鏡），無眼部不適
4 聽力正常
5 無腦部損傷、癲癇等神經系統疾病
6 右利手（如書寫、使用餐具習慣使用右手）
7未曾參與過本研究相關實驗（如不確定，可聯絡主試確認：Miss RAO, 1155197282@link.cuhk.edu.hk)
报名链接：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_d6DwKRrT43upfSu
我們將在WhatsAPP聯繫符合要求的小朋友參與測試。所有數據絕對保密，僅用於學術研究。
香港中文大學語言學及現代語言系
如有問題，請聯絡饒女士（
1155197282@link.cuhk.edu.hk
）
This research is endorsed by
Prof. CAI Zhenguang
zhenguangcai@cuhk.edu.hk
Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
English Version:
Do you know your child’s traditional Chinese character reading and writing ability? Don’t miss this fun and meaningful research opportunity!
By taking part in this study, your child can not only receive compensation but also bring home a lovely gift!
Study Tasks:
We are inviting Primary 4 students (who have just completed Grade 4 and are about to begin Grade 5) to take part in writing and reading tasks in Traditional Chinese. We will use specialized equipment to record writing trajectories and pressure, and assess reading and language abilities through interactive language games.
Duration:
Approximately 2 hours
Location:
Leung Kau Kui Building (Department of Linguistics), The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Compensation:
Participants will receive HKD 400 in cash, along with a set of Chiikawa stationery gifts
Eligibility Requirements:
A fourth-grade student (just finished fourth grade and is about to start fifth grade).
Receiving Chinese instruction in Traditional Chinese and Cantonese at school
Normal vision (glasses allowed), with no eye discomfort
Normal hearing
No history of neurological conditions (e.g., brain injury, epilepsy)
Right-handed (e.g., writing and using utensils with the right hand)
Have not participated in related studies of this project (if unsure, please contact the researcher: Miss Rao,
1155197282@link.cuhk.edu.hk
)
Registration:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_d6DwKRrT43upfSu
Eligible participants will be contacted via
WhatsApp
to arrange the session. All data is strictly confidential and used only for academic research.
Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
The Chinese University of Hong Kong

Miss Rao (
1155197282@link.cuhk.edu.hk
)
This research is endorsed by
Prof. CAI Zhenguang

bodyText:

Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/07/17
»
Seminars / Forums / Programmes / Workshops
The Independent Learning Centre (ILC) offers a wide range of workshops and activities to support learning of language and communication skills. Visit our website for more information: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ (20260720)  - ILC
From: ILC
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ilc-counsel@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
【Weekly Highlights - English Section 】
A. Communication, Study Skills and Job Preparation Workshops
The Independent Learning Centre offers English workshops 20 July to 24 July: (1) Academic Reading: Strategies for Success, (2) Building a Bigger and Better Vocabulary, (3) Job Preparation Series: Ace Your In-person and Video Job Interviews, and (4) Listening to Learn: Academic Listening and Note-taking Skills. These workshops are now available for registration at: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/workshops.aspx
B. Consultation Service in English
Consultation service is available during the following time:
20 July (Mon): 14:30 – 16:30
21 July (Tue): 14:30 – 16:30
22 July (Wed): 10:30 – 12:30
23 July (Thu): 10:30 – 12:30
24 July (Fri): 14:30 – 16:30
Online Booking:
https://ilccuhk.as.me/schedule.php
More Timeslot please check our website：
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EH/consultation.aspx
====================================
【Weekly Highlights - Chinese Section 】中文部本週活動
A. Chinese Workshops 中文工作坊
The Independent Learning Centre offers Chinese workshops 20 July to 24 July: (1) Cantonese Interview Skills, (2) Preparation for the JRE: How to write government official letters, (3) JRE Argumentative Writing I, and (4) An introduction to the ancient Chinese military treatise: Sunzi the Art of War (PTH). These workshops are now available for registration at: https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/workshops.aspx
自學中心七月二十日至七月二十四日舉辦 (1) 粵語面試技巧, (2) 粵語平仄與近體詩及對聯, (3) JRE政府公函寫作, (4) JRE 議論文寫作 (一), (5) 「信而好古」——粵語與中國古代文化 （粵）, 及 (6) 古兵法略說：孫子 (普)等工作坊，歡迎報名。
登記連結： https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/workshops.aspx
B. Consultation Service in Chinese 自學中心中文輔導服務
Consultation service is available during the following time:
自學中心於七月二十日至七月二十四日提供以下中文輔導時段。
21 July (Tue): 10:30 – 12:30
22 July (Wed): 10:30 – 12:30 and 14:30 – 16:30
23 July (Thu): 14:30 – 16:30
網上預約：
https://ilccuhk.as.me/schedule.php
更多中文輔導時段。
====================================
C. “The Power of Words” 「書寫力量」
This is a reading and writing event organized by the ILC, Hong Kong Literature Research Centre, the Office of Arts Administrator (OAA) and Tolopoem. Activities we have this semester include Blackboard / Glass Wall Poems, Talks of Dialogue in the Arts and Workshops.
自學中心、香港文學研究中心、藝術行政主任辦公室及吐露詩社合辦的大型閱讀及寫作活動。這個學期的活動，除黑板詩及玻璃詩外，還有藝文縱談及各式工作坊。各項活動的資料可以參看：https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/Event/thepowerofwords.aspx
====================================
【Independent Online Learning Resources】自學中心網上自學資源
A. Independent Online Learning Resources in English
- Academic Writing
Visit this link on academic writing skills and convention for different citation styles:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/Writing_Writing.aspx
- Vocabulary
Visit this link for both General Vocabulary and Specific Vocabulary (e.g. For Business and Medical Professionals) lists and practices:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/Writing_Vocab.aspx
- Job Search and Interviews
Visit this link to identify your capabilities and personality types, learn how to prepare job search documents and personal statements, and how to get ready for job interviews:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/JobSearching.aspx
B. Independent Online Learning Resources in Chinese中文網上自學材料
- Academic Writing論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on academic writing, with highlights on structure, expressions, common grammatical mistakes, etc.
針對大學生撰寫學術論文時所遇到的困難，提供實用的知識和練習。內容包括：學期論文的結構與寫作步驟、常見語法錯誤、表達與語言邏輯等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/AWOnline/general1.html
- ‘Pulewang’ Online Putonghua Platform「普樂網」網上普通話平台
An online Putonghua learning platform designed for CU students. Essential knowledge of Putonghua is introduced with interactive exercises and games. Extended conversational exchanges on selected topics of social affairs and student life are available for oral practice with texts and pinyin.
針對本校同學學習需要的網上普通話平台，內容圍繞大學生的學習與日常生活，設計深入淺出，每單元均有練習與遊戲，互動有趣，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Chinese/plw/index.html
- Argumentative Writing議論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on the structure, the content and the language of argumentative writing.
介紹議論文的結構及寫作要求，以解說、例子及練習，呈現寫作議論時要注意的內容及語言特點：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/arguWriting/001.html
- Cantonese Pronunciation粵語拼音速遞
This guide is designed for mainland students as an effective way to learn Cantonese pronunciation. Basic knowledge of Cantonese syllables is introduced with exercises. Comparison of Cantonese and Putonghua pronunciation is also highlighted
協助內地同學迅速掌握粵語發音。內容包括：語音基礎、粵普對比、難點練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/cantontones/_home/index.html
- Cantonese Express港式粵語速遞
An interactive introduction to Hong Kong style Cantonese. Daily expressions and situational conversations are introduced with interactive exercises.
以有趣互動的方式介紹港式粵語，包括日常生活用語、情景會話、互動練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/canton_express/others/frontpage.html
- Online Cantonese for Foreigners
A free online platform for international students to learn basic Cantonese. The texts are clear and simple, and interactive exercises easy to use: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/can_eng/layout.html
- Online Putonghua for Foreigners
Do you know how to make orders in a Chinese restaurant and learn how to bargain when you travel in China? Here are some situational conversations and basic knowledge of Putonghua to learn online: https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/CHResources/Lang_PTH_EnglishSpk.aspx
- Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) 中國語言及文化自學資源網
Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) is a biliterate (English and Chinese) online platform that contains reviews of learning materials suitable for autodidactic study in the 5 big areas of Mandarin, Cantonese, Chinese Characters, Chinese Culture, and Hong Kong Culture. Electronic learning materials that is good for self-learning would be review. Each review consists of a description and other useful information. Users can search for resources by various criteria, rate the resources, and write their own comments. A self-assessment system is also provided so as to recommend an entry point to the users according to their current level.
中國語言及文化自學資源網(OPSCL)為一推薦自學資源之網上平台。平台為有意學習普通話、粵語、漢字、中國文化或香港文化等五大範疇的人士提供中文及英文雙語之學習資源，以推動自主學習與終身學習。平台內推薦的資源均附有簡介及評語，使用者可按自身需要搜尋學習資源，並在使用後給予評分或評論，以備其他使用者參考。此外，平台設有「自評系統」，使用者可通過完成自評，確定自身的學習起步點，從而尋找適合自己程度的學習資源。

From: Learning and Cultural Enhancement Section

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
The International Connection Programme (ICP) is a cross-cultural peer mentorship programme organized by the Office of Student Affairs, which offers a unique opportunity for students from diverse backgrounds to connect and enhance cultural understanding. We warmly invite you to join us as a mentor, where you will have the chance to:
Build intercultural mentoring networks by connecting with incoming non-local students
Develop and enhance your global leadership skills
Broaden your cultural exposure and contribute to a more culturally inclusive and diverse campus
Eligibility
All Year 2-or-above full-time undergraduate students who will be studying at CUHK in both terms of 2026-27.
Online interviews in late August
will be required.
Matching
In each group, two mentors will be matched up with three to four mentees. Matching will be conducted based on factors such as personal interests, major, affiliated college.
Content
1. Connection Session for Mentors
All mentors will be required to attend the session:
Date: Early September 2026
Time: 6:30pm – 8:30pm (tentative)
Location: CUHK
Content: Meeting your partner mentor, connecting with fellow mentors, and gaining a deeper understanding of the mentor role and the programme
2. Training Day Camp
All participants will be required to attend the training day camp:
Date: 4 October 2026 (Sunday)
Time: 9:00am – 4:00pm (Round-trip transportation will be arranged)
Location: Tai Po
Content: Ice-breaking, team building, cross-cultural communication skills, global leadership development
3. Bonding and cultural activities initiated by your group
4. Engaging cultural events organized by the Office of Student Affairs
5.
Visit to CUHK (Shenzhen)
6. Leadership and Cultural tour
Certification and Prize
Student Development Portfolio (SDP) record update
Certificate of Appreciation (Requirement: attendance in the training day camp, one LCES-endorsed activity, completion of self-initiated cultural activity and submission of report)
Cultural tour in 2027
(For selected teams)
Opportunity to be nominated for the CUHK Outstanding Students Awards
Apply now to be part of this enriching initiative!

2026-2027 Voluntary User-Pay Dental Service Scheme (VUPDSS)
Voluntary User-Pay Dental Service Scheme (VUPDSS) is a voluntary and self-paid dental service between the University’s members and the service providers, Health & Care Dental Services Limited or Quality HealthCare Dental Services Limited. Its primary purpose is to provide participants the additional convenience of receiving dental service at contracted dental clinics outside campus at concessionary rate. Full-time students, full-time staff and dependents, eligible retirees and dependents can enroll in the Scheme. The Scheme is open for application. Membership is valid from 1 Sep 2026 to 31 August 2027.
Details of the Scheme is available at:
https://www.umso.cuhk.edu.hk/form-download/
2026-2027 自費牙科服務計劃
「自費牙科服務計劃」為一個自願性付費形式的牙齒保健計劃。 合資格大學成員可參加由恒健牙科服務有限公司或卓健牙科服務有限公司所提供的牙科保健服務。 本計劃旨在為參加者提供一個具彈性及享有優惠價格之牙科服務。 全日制學生、全職職員及家屬、合資格退休員工及家屬均可參加。 計劃現正接受申請，會籍有效期由2026年9月1日至2027年8月31日。
計劃詳情，請瀏覽網頁:
https://www.umso.cuhk.edu.hk/hk/form-download/

title: [$200 travel allowance] Recruiting aged 65 or above, along with their caregivers, to join an interview on elderly physical and mental health. [$200交通津貼] 招募年滿65歲的香港居民及其照顧者參加訪問調查，以了解香港長者的身心健康
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/07/17
»
Announcements
[$200 travel allowance] Recruiting aged 65 or above, along with their caregivers, to join an interview on elderly physical and mental health.  [$200交通津貼] 招募年滿65歲的香港居民及其照顧者參加訪問調查，以了解香港長者的身心健康 - JC School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: Amy Wong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
amy.wong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
***
中文版本
***
研究背景
香港中文大學現正進行一項有關長者身心健康的調查，從而制定一個可以測量長者健康生活品質的工具。
招募對象
長者：65歲或以上，照顧者：18歲或以上；
香港居民；
能閱讀中文及以廣東話溝通； 及
曾使用長者服務設施或入住護理之家
參與方式
如果符合上述條件，請在下方連結登記及留下相關資料以作跟進，需時約1-3分鐘。完成登記後，研究人員將於兩星期內與你聯絡，並安排你與被照顧的長者以面對面形式完成訪問。
答謝安排
個人訪問約需時 30-40 分鐘。完成訪問後，長者與照顧者合共可獲港幣 200 元現金以作答謝。每位參加者只限參加一次。
報名登記連結
:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_00u21fpHbgdjKuO
查詢
本研究已獲香港中文大學 —
調查及行為研究操守委員會
的審批。 (參考編號: SBRE-25-0737) 。如有任何查詢，歡迎聯絡主研究員 黃麗儀教授 (電郵:
lywong@cuhk.edu.hk
) 或研究員黃小姐 (Amy) / 張小姐 (Annie) (電話: 2252-8408 / 2252-8404) 。
名額有限！先到先得！
歡迎轉發此訊息給您的家人及朋友！
***
English version
***
S
tudy Background
The JC School of Public Health and Primary Care at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently conducting an interview on the physical and mental health of older adults in Hong Kong to develop a tool in measuring their health-related quality of life in Hong Kong.
Target Group
Elderly: Aged 65 or above; Caregiver: 18 years old or above;
Hong Kong residents;
Able to read Chinese and communicate in Cantonese; and
Has ever used elderly service facilities or nursing homes.
How to Participate
If you meet the above criteria, please complete the registration form in around 1-3 minutes. After registration, our staff will contact you within two weeks and arrange an in-person interview for you and the elderly participant to complete.
Appreciation
The individual interview takes about 30-40 minutes. Upon completion, you and the elderly participant will receive a total of HK$200 cash as a token of appreciation. Each participant may only participate once.
Registration L
ink:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_00u21fpHbgdjKuO
Contact Us
This study has been approved by the Survey and Behavioural Research Ethics Committee (Ref: SBRE-25-0737). Should you have any enquiries, please contact the Principal Investigator Prof. Eliza Wong (E-mail: lywong@cuhk.edu.hk), or researchers Ms. Amy Wong or Ms. Annie Cheung (Tel: 2252-8408 / 2252-8404).
Limited quotas only! First come, first served!
Feel free to share this invitation with your family and friends!
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

title: Join us for Geoscience Workshop 2026! 齊齊來參加地球科學工作坊 2026！
bodyText:

Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/07/17
»
Events / Activities
Join us for Geoscience Workshop 2026! 齊齊來參加地球科學工作坊 2026！ - CUHK Library
From: The Chinese University of Hong Kong Library
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
liblc@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
地球科學工作坊
2026
香港中文大學地球與環境科學系聯同大學圖書館及香港地質學會 誠邀您參加 地球科學工作坊 2026。本活動將展示來自世界各地的岩石樣本，帶領參加者探索礦物與岩石的奧秘，了解地質學家如何解讀地球運作的方式與演化歷程。現場更設有 VR、AR 及互動遊戲，讓您以輕鬆有趣的方式學習地球科學原理，體驗像地質學家一樣思考的樂趣。

詳情及報名：
https://forms.cloud.microsoft/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=gTdBhKa7s0W74E8XxpDaaomlJowqRi9Ige7_IcBW0K9UMkJaQVkzS1hZSTJIQ1hETERKUTY3NTNVNS4u
如有任何查詢，請電郵至
eesc@cuhk.edu.hk
或
tampuiyuk@cuhk.edu.hk
。
期待在地球科學工作坊 2026 與您相見。
Geoscience Workshop 2026
The Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences, CUHK, in collaboration with the CUHK Library and the Geological Society of Hong Kong, is pleased to invite you to Geoscience Workshop 2026. This event will showcase rock samples from around the world and guide participants in exploring the fascinating world of minerals and rocks, while learning how geologists interpret Earth’s processes and history through geological evidence.
The workshop will also feature VR, AR, and interactive games, offering a fun and engaging way to learn the principles of geoscience and experience the excitement of “think like a geologist”.

Details and registration:
https://forms.cloud.microsoft/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=gTdBhKa7s0W74E8XxpDaaomlJowqRi9Ige7_IcBW0K9UMkJaQVkzS1hZSTJIQ1hETERKUTY3NTNVNS4u
For enquiries, please email
eesc@cuhk.edu.hk
or
tampuiyuk@cuhk.edu.hk
.
We look forward to welcoming you to Geoscience Workshop 2026.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

Student Helper Recruitment for Inauguration Ceremony for Undergraduates 2026
學生事務處現為二零二六年本科生入學典禮招募學生助手。詳情如下︰
日期︰二零二六年九月七日（星期一）
工作時間︰早上八時三十分至十一時三十分
工作地點︰中大校園內
工作性質︰一）確保入學典禮正常進行；二）協助場地佈置及收拾場地；三）協助疏導人流；四）點算參加者人數；五）解答一般查詢；六）按現場需要協助本處職員處理其他相關工作
時薪︰港幣六十七元正
請注意，獲選同學必須出席八月十四日（星期五）下午的兩小時工作講解會。講解會將不會計入工作時數內。
如有意申請成為學生助手，請於二零二六年七月八日（星期三）前完成及遞交
本登記表格
。如有任何疑問，請致電 39433767（司徒先生）或 39437210（潘女士）查詢。
The Office of Student Affairs is recruiting student helpers for The Inauguration Ceremony for Undergraduate 2026 event support. Details as below.
Date: 7 September 2026 (Monday)
Time: 8:30 am – 11:30 am
Venue: CUHK campus
Duties: 1) Support Inauguration Ceremony; 2) Assist in venue set up and dismantle; 3) Crowd control management; 4) Taking attendance record; 5) Handle enquiry and 6) Any other on-site support tasks as assigned by OSA staff
Hour Rate: HK$ 67/ hr
Please note selected applicants must attend a 2-hrs briefing session on 14 August afternoon. The briefing session will be excluded from student helper work hours.
Please complete and submit
this registration form
by 7 August 2026 (Wednesday) if you would like to apply for the opening. For enquiry, please contact Mr. Szeto at 39433767 or Miss Poon at 39437210.

Announcements
Participants Wanted for a Cross-Cultural Sleep Study (15-minute questionnaire with a chance to receive an HKD $100 cash voucher!) 招募參與跨文化睡眠研究參加者 (15分鐘問卷，有機會獲得$100現金券！） - Department of Psychology
From: Lo Eugene
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
eugenelo@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
招募參與跨文化睡眠研究參加者 (15分鐘問卷，有機會獲得$100現金券！）
研究概要：
本研究旨在了解不同文化背景下，人們如何理解及詮釋睡眠癱瘓（俗稱「鬼壓床」）及相關睡眠感知經驗。
透過參與本研究，您可以幫助我們了解睡眠習慣、文化信念及感官體驗如何影響人們對這些特殊睡眠經驗的理解，以及不同文化之間的差異。
本研究由杜倫大學（Durham University）與香港中文大學心理學系合作進行。
參加資格：
• 18歲或以上人士
• 現為英國或香港的大學生
• 具基本閱讀英文的能力
• 沒有神經系統疾病（例如癲癇）
• 沒有藥物或酒精濫用問題
• 不需要曾經歷睡眠癱瘓（鬼壓床）
研究詳情：
參加者需完成一份約15分鐘的網上問卷，內容包括：
• 睡眠癱瘓或相關睡眠經驗
• 睡眠及午睡習慣
• 感官與知覺體驗
• 對超自然或科學解釋的看法
潛在風險：
本研究預期不會有任何潛在風險。
研究回饋：
30位完成問卷者將於九月隨機抽出，每人可獲港幣$100現金券。
所有參與均屬自願性質，所有作答內容將被嚴格保密，並只供研究用途。
如有興趣參與研究，請掃描 QR Code
或填寫問卷連結。
https://durhambs.az1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6gxhPknKBxTHAQS
如對本研究有任何查詢，歡迎聯絡：
Mr. Lee Yau Wai
dhhl12@durham.ac.uk
Participants Wanted for a Cross-Cultural Sleep Study
(15-minute questionnaire with a chance to receive an HKD $100 cash voucher!)
Research Overview:
This study aims to explore how people from different cultural backgrounds understand and interpret sleep paralysis (commonly referred to as the “Sleep Paralysis Demon” or “Ghost Oppression”) and related sleep-related perceptual experiences.
By participating in this study, you can help us better understand how sleep habits, cultural beliefs, and sensory experiences influence people’s interpretations of these unusual sleep experiences across cultures.
This research is conducted collaboratively by Durham University and the Department of Psychology at The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Eligibility:
• Aged 18 or above
• Currently a university student in the UK or Hong Kong
• Able to read English
• No neurological disorders (e.g. epilepsy)
• No drug or alcohol abuse problems
• You do not need to have experienced sleep paralysis before
Study Details:
Participants will complete an online questionnaire that takes approximately 15 minutes. The questionnaire includes:
• Sleep paralysis or related sleep experiences
• Sleep and napping habits
• Sensory and perceptual experiences
• Beliefs about supernatural or scientific explanations
Potential risk:
No potential risks are anticipated in the study.
Participant Reward:
30 participants who complete the questionnaire will be randomly selected in September to receive an HKD $100 cash voucher.
Participation in this study is entirely voluntary. All responses will be kept strictly confidential and used for research purposes only.
If you are interested, please register at the following link or scan the QR code below:
https://durhambs.az1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6gxhPknKBxTHAQS
If you have any enquiries, please contact:
Mr. Lee Yau Wai
dhhl12@durham.ac.uk

From: Office of Academic Links (Mainland and Regional)

為進一步促進大灣區學術合作，香港中文大學將於2026年7月31日（星期五）， 以線上線下結合的形式， 舉辦2026年大灣區科學論壇名師講堂，並很榮幸邀請到嚴純華院士、陳清泉院士分享真知灼見，並與粵港澳大灣區的青年科學家進行對話，深入交流討論關於求知、為學、創新、研究管理的經驗，及人生哲學與倫理，進一步培養有全面性思想的國家未來科創人才。
日期：2026年7月31日（星期五）
時間：上午9:40–12:30
地點：香港中文大學康本國際學術園地下演講廳LT3
報名：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13712130
To further promote academic collaboration in the Greater Bay Area, The Chinese University of Hong Kong will host the 2026 Greater Bay Area Science Forum Distinguished Lecture on July 31, 2026 (Friday), in a hybrid format combining online and offline participation. We are honored to invite Academician Yan Chunhua and Academician Chan Ching-chuen to share their insights and engage in dialogue with young scientists from the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. This event aims to facilitate in-depth discussions on knowledge acquisition, learning, innovation, research management, as well as life philosophy and ethics, further nurturing well-rounded future talents for the nation’s scientific and technological innovation.
Date: 31 July 2026 (Friday)
Time: 9:40am - 12:30pm
Venue: LT3, G/F, Yasumoto International Academic Park, CUHK
Registration：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13712130
View Count

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

The Infectious Disease Research Team at JC School of Public Health and Primary Care, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK), invites CUHK students to join us. Our team is led by experienced public health experts dedicated to cutting-edge health-related research. We now recruit student helpers to support research duties, including data entry, recruitment, and administration. You will see how scientific studies operate behind the scenes.

Responsibilities:

bodyText:

Announcements
Invitation to Participate in a Survey on Advance Medical Directives (Medical Students)  - CUHK Centre for Bioethics
From: CUHK Centre for Bioethics
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
bioethics@med.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Dear Students,
You are cordially invited to participate in a survey study jointly led by Prof. Emmanuel Cheung (Critical Care Medicine Unit, University of Hong Kong) and Dr. Ann Lau (Centre for Bioethics, The Chinese University of Hong Kong).
As you may be aware, the Advance Decision on Life-sustaining Treatment Ordinance will come into effect on 31 July 2026. This study seeks to explore medical students’ knowledge and preparedness to engage in advance care planning and end-of-life discussions.
The survey is anonymous, and participation is entirely voluntary. It will take around 10 minutes to complete. Only aggregate data will be reported.
Eligibility:
All medical students enrolled in HKU (MBBS) and CUHK (MBChB).
Survey Link:
https://hku.au1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eW35gjGnwzz98iy
This study has been reviewed and received ethics clearance from the Human Research Ethics Committee of the University of Hong Kong (EA250716).
If you have any questions about the research, please feel free to contact Prof. Emmanuel Cheung (
ehcheung@hku.hk
), or Dr. Ann Lau (
annsnlau@cuhk.edu.hk
).
We greatly appreciate your valuable input and contribution to this important area of study.
Sincerely,

mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
or WhatsApp: (+852-53202853).

From: Phoebe Chan
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學精神科學系正進行一項研究，主要探討運用語音分析檢測青少年的憂鬱症狀。現招募年齡介乎18歲至24歲的青少年參與研究，歡迎所有健康人士、抑鬱和焦慮人士參加。詳情如下:
我們誠邀符合以下條件的人士參與本次研究：
18歲至24歲青少年,
除了抑鬱和焦慮外，沒有確診其他精神障礙
能說流利的廣東話
使用智慧型手機（附錄音機）並可持續存取互聯網
接受本研究所使用的即時通訊應用程式的服務條款和隱私權政策
您需要做什麼？
通過篩查訪談後，在手機
連續 7 天
使用指定的訊息應用程式
使用手機上的錄音功能進行數位語音錄音，包括（a）指定的段落閱讀和（b）引導音訊日記。
每天
早上
和
晚上
，在應用程式分別回答4個指導性問題
進行跟進訪談
完成實驗及跟進評估後，可以獲得$200現金津貼。
有興趣的參加者請按以下連結填寫問卷：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_801s3xAKvKm1Uma
研究員將通過WhatsApp聯絡合適的參加者，並詳細解釋研究內容。
閣下留下的資料僅供研究用途，絕對保密。如閣下對是項研究有任何查詢，請電郵
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
或 WhatsApp:(+852- 53202853)。
For participants who are interested, please click the link below to complete the questionnaire:

Announcements
<HK$300>Brain Health Study  <HK$300>中大醫學院邀您參與腦部健康研究 - CUHK Psychiatry Sleep Assessment Unit
From: Wong Yuen Tung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
yuentungwong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
便秘？嗅覺變差？睡覺拳打腳踢？有腦退化家族史？
這些看似平常的小毛病，其實可能是柏金遜症等大腦退化的早期先兆！
提早了解大腦健康，預防神經退化！
中大醫學院睡眠研究小組推出全新手機篩查App，誠邀您參與醫學研究！
研究對象：
年齡介乎
50 至 65 歲
的華人
未確診
任何腦神經退化疾病（如柏金遜症、阿爾茲海默症/失智症等）
參加者需完成以下程序：
參與研究

bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/07/17
»
Events / Activities
Water Sports Training Course (Sailing & Windsurfing) - CUHK Water Sports Centre 水上活動訓練課程 (風帆及滑浪風帆) - 中大水上活動中心 - Water Sports Centre / P E Unit
From: Kent Wong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
kentwong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
(The English version follows the Chinese one)
============ 中大水上活動中心通訊 =============
***** 訓練課程 *****
(更多資料: http://www.facebook.com/WSC.CUHK)
初級滑浪風帆訓練班 (兩天課程) (適合初學人仕參與)
* 8月29(六)及30 (日) (W6)
風帆入門訓練班 (第一級) (兩天課程)
* 8月22 (六)及23 (日) (S5)
# 為提供更完善的服務給您、中大不同部門及其他學會對水上活動的需要，本中心現特設 "度身訂造" 服務，馬上致電2603 6776聯絡我們吧!
***** 報名方式 *****
(更多資料: https://tinyurl.com/kxp3dwm2 or http://www.facebook.com/WSC.CUHK)
網上報名日期：
Class S5及W6 - 由2026年7月17日 (星期五) 下午5:30至7月20日 (星期一) 下午3:00，先到先得，額滿即止。
網上報名網址：
https://webapp.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/ras/restricted/eventlist?id=73
# 查詢請致電2603 6776 (水上活動中心辦事處)。
***** 人數上限 *****
(更多資料: http://www.facebook.com/WSC.CUHK)
+ 滑浪風帆訓練班：上限5人
+ 風帆訓練班：上限6人
***** 收費 *****
(更多資料: http://www.facebook.com/WSC.CUHK)
+ 滑浪風帆訓練班：
** 初級課程 - 學生$630, 職員 (及家屬) $700
+ 風帆入門訓練班：
** 第一級 - 學生$680, 職員 (及家屬) $740
體育部將津貼滑浪風帆及風帆訓練班($200)予全期出席之學生，退款將於課程後即時退回。
注意：
參加者需懂泳術，學員或須通過水試（於第一天穿著衣服及救生衣游畢50米）。
所有水上活動課程需要有一定體能要求。
教學語言，粵語輔以英語。
如參與獨木舟二星或以上級別訓練課程，參加者必須於上課時出示有關證明文件，否則將不獲受理。
參加者必須年滿14歲；18歲以下人士參加者必須於得到家長/監護人/授權人簽署及同意；16歲以下人士參加者必須由家長/監護人/授權人陪同。家長/監護人/授權人必須年滿18歲。
所繳之費用包括教練及需用器材，完成證書課程並合格者，將獲發證書，證書費需另外繳付，獨木舟證書為$45，滑浪風帆$30及風帆證書為$115/$55。
所有項目一經報名，不得申請退款（包括因病）、轉班或由他人代替參加（如天氣惡劣、人數不足及中心宣佈課程取消除外）。
課程當天直接到大學水上活動中心集合，自備泳裝、可浸水運動鞋（包趾及腳跟）、長袖衣服及午餐。
報名人數未及名額之班別將會取消，各有關之參加者將獲電郵個別通知。
體育部將津貼獨木舟訓練班($90)及風帆訓練班($200)予全期出席之學生，退款將於課程後即時退回。
查詢電話：水上活動中心2603-6776   大學體育中心3943-6097
******* News for the Water Sports Training Course *******
Basic Windsurfing Training Course (2-day course) (It also fit for Improver):
* 29-30 Aug (Sat & Sun) (W6)
Introduction to Sailing Training Course (Level 1) (2-day course)
* 22-23Aug (Sat & Sun) (S5)
- The Centre offers a tailored package for all CUHK members (services include a fun day, a certificate course, and a special event); for more information, please call 2603 6776 (CUWSC Office).
******* Enrollment *******
Online enrollment will be accepted on a first-come, first-served basis until the course reaches its maximum capacity.
Class S5 & W6 - 5:30 pm on 17 Jul to 3:00 pm on 20 Jul 2026
Direct register link for user:
https://webapp.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/ras/restricted/eventlist?id=73
******* Max capacity *******
+ Windsurfing Training Course: Max. 5 persons
+ Sailing Training Course: Max. 6 persons
******* Course fee *******
+ Windsurfing Training Course:
- Student ($630), Staff & Family member ($700)
+ Introduction to Sailing Training Course (Level 1):
- Student ($680), Staff & Family member ($740)
Physical Education Unit will subsidize STUDENT with 100% attendance in Kayaking Training Course ($90) and Windsurfing / Sailing Training Course ($200). Subsidize will be refunded after the course except for abstention.
******** Contact us **********
Further information will be posted to Water Sports Centre Website (https://tinyurl.com/kxp3dwm2 or http://www.facebook.com/WSC.CUHK), University Sports Centre notice board. We are welcome any inquiry kentwong@cuhk.edu.hk (email) & 2603 6776(OFFICE)
Remarks:
Participants are required to swim 50 meters with clothes and a life jacket. A water test may be required on Day 1.
Participants should be aware that water sports require a certain level of physical fitness.
Language: Cantonese supplemented with English.
When participating Kayak 2 Star Award or above level, participants MUST be required to show the related certification. If not, the Centre may not accept the enrollment.
Participants must be at least 14 years of age; Participants under the age of 18 must obtain parent / guardian / authorized person signed and agreed; Participants under the age of 16 must be parent / guardian / authorized person accompanied. Parents / guardians / authorized person must be 18 years of age.
The course fee covers only the instructor fee and equipment. Participants who successfully complete and pass the course exam will receive a certificate. The certificate with a logbook cost $45 for kayaking, $30 for windsurfing and $55/$115 for sailing.
Refunds, program changes, or participant substitutions are not permitted after enrollment (including those due to illness), except in cases of bad weather, insufficient participants, or cancellations announced by the Centre.
On the course day, participants will be gathered at Water Sports Centre. Swimsuit, long sleeves shirt, and a pair of sports shoes (Close toe and heel) that will be used in water and lunch needed to be prepared by self.
The course will be cancelled upon insufficient enrollment. The involved participants will be notified by email individually.
Physical Education Unit will subsidize STUDENT with 100% attendance in Windsurfing / Sailing Training ($200). Subsidize will be refunded after the course except abstention.
For enquiries, please call Water Sports Centre at 2603-6776 or Physical Education Unit at 3943-6097.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

AI and Music!! Recruiting Young Music Lovers | AI and Popular Song Emotion Categorization Research AI同Music!!招募音樂愛好青年｜人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Xiuyang Meng
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk

招募音樂愛好青年｜人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究
我們正在尋找熱愛音樂的你，參與人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究，用你的聽感為 AI 模型注入真實的青年情緒視角。
研究目的
本研究旨在運用人工智能技術，從青年視角對粵語流行歌曲進行情緒分類標註，評估青年群體對音樂情緒的主觀感知特徵，並為個性化音樂推薦系統及情緒調節相關研究提供數據支持。
招募條件
18 至 24 歲，熱愛音樂且經常聆聽流行音樂，能流暢使用粵語及英語進行溝通與表達的青年。
參與內容
聆聽 50 首粵語流行歌曲，並完整聽畢每首參與標註的曲目，依據自身主觀體驗與即時情緒感受，將歌曲進行情緒分類。
如何加入？
請點擊以下連結進行註冊，並回答幾條簡單問題。研究員將聯絡適合的參加者，詳細解釋研究內容：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5pU67FrIxYilalw
聯絡我們
如有任何疑問，請於辦公時間內致電 6115-0322 與研究助理陳小姐 或 蒙先生聯絡。
Recruiting Young Music Lovers | AI and Popular Song Emotion Categorization Research
We are looking for music lovers like you to participate in our research on AI and popular song emotion categorization, contributing your listening experience to inject authentic youth emotional perspectives into our AI model.
Purpose of the Study
This study aims to use artificial intelligence technology to annotate the emotion categories of Cantopop songs from a youth perspective, evaluate the subjective emotional perception characteristics of young people towards music, and provide data support for personalized music recommendation systems and emotion regulation-related research.
Eligibility Criteria
Young people aged 18 to 24 who love music, listen to popular music regularly, and are able to communicate fluently in Cantonese and English.
Participation Content
Listen to 50 Cantopop songs in full, and categorize each song according to your subjective experience and immediate emotional feelings.
How to Join?
Please click the link below to register and answer a few simple questions. Our researchers will contact eligible participants to explain the study details in full:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5pU67FrIxYilalw
Contact Us
If you have any questions, please call 6115-0322 during office hours to speak with our research assistants Ms. Chan or Mr. Meng.
View Count

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

From: Donald Liu
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
donaldliu@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
靜觀課程對有慢性壓力的長者的微生物群成效研究: 隨機對照試驗
Effects of mindfulness-based training on the microbiome of older adults with chronic stress: A randomised controlled trial
現正誠邀合資格人士報名參加
We are now recruiting participants to join our programme.
賽馬會公共衛生及基層醫療學院 現誠邀60歲以上人士參加一項靜觀課程研究
研究將會探討靜觀課程對有慢性壓力的長者的微生物群的影響。
很多長者受慢性壓力困擾，如未能適當處理壓力，對他們的心理及生理皆有嚴重影響。研究發現慢性壓力會破壞腸道微生物群的平衡。靜觀證實可有效改善心理健康，卻甚少研究探究靜觀課程如何改善參與者的微生物群。這項研究將在社區招募138名年滿60歲人士，邀請他們參與為長者而設的靜觀課程與健康教育控制課程，比較兩者於改善壓力、負面情緒及腸道微生物的成效。
參加者將會被隨機分派入兩組其中一組：
a) 靜觀練習組：
分派入本組的參加者將接受為期八周，每週一次，每次大約一小時三十分鐘的靜觀課程。每堂靜課程將會錄音，以作審視課程的保真度。
b) 健康教育組：
分派入本組的參加者會接受為期八周，每週一次，每次大約一小時三十分鐘的健康教育課程，課程內容包括營養，運動，維持生活習慣。每堂靜課程將會錄音，以作審視課程的保真度。
招募對象:
i) 年齡60歲以上;
ii) 能聽講廣東話;
iii) 需要持續照顧有長期病患的親屬;

Want
M365 Copilot
to nail it on the first try? The secret is
constraints
! Adding specific limits — word count, format, audience level, do/don’t rules — dramatically improves the output. Think of constraints as guardrails that keep Copilot on the exact road you want.
Try this prompt — copy & paste it!
“Write a safety reminder announcement for our warehouse team about proper lifting techniques. Constraints: (1) Maximum 100 words, (2)
Writing style: Clear and simple
, (3) Include exactly 3 key safety tips, (4) End with a memorable safety slogan, (5) Do NOT use technical terminology, (6) Format as a poster-ready text with a bold title.”
Why this works:
Each constraint acts like a guardrail — the more specific your boundaries, the less guesswork Copilot has to do, and the closer the output matches your exact needs.

Bonus tip:
Useful constraints to try: “Use bullet points only”, “Write for a non-technical audience”, “Keep each paragraph under 3 sentences”, “Include a call to action”, “Use active voice only.”

for even more helpful guidance and best practices.

「重塑榕樹凹：共創山海村落」—
地方營造大使招募
中文大學建築學院現正推動一項以「鄉郊地方營造（Rural Placemaking）」為核心的鄉村學堂及暑期工作坊，誠邀熱愛香港鄉郊文化、樂於親身參與實作的你，一同走進榕樹凹，參與村落景觀的復育與共創行動。
計劃期間，我們將邀請香港建造學院團隊擔任導師，帶領參加者學習傳統建造工藝及鄉郊實踐技術。參加者可自選出席一天或多天工作坊。若完成九天的工作坊後，參加者將獲頒由中文大學建築學院及香港建造學院簽發之服務證書，以作嘉許。
榕樹凹介紹：
榕樹凹位於新界東北端，於三百多年前開基立村，是一條歷史悠久的客家溫姓村落，村落鼎盛時期曾有逾三百名居民。由於地理位置接近邊境，榕樹凹在1980年代曾設有英軍軍營，留下了一段獨特而鮮為人知的歷史印記。雖然村落現已無人居住，但村民近年積極推動復村工作，透過修復祖屋、整理村史、舉辦村宴及傳統儀式，如籌辦麒麟隊；重建社群連結與文化記憶，展現出對深厚的鄉土感情與文化傳承精神。
****************************************
願景
共創鄉郊地方營造：以低碳修復與地方記憶，重塑山海景觀。
空間實作：以小型建設改善路徑與休憩空間。
感官敘事：將歷史轉化為具體的景觀導覽。
​共創行動：透過行動連結設計思考與鄉村振興。
****************************************
活動地點： 新界沙頭角榕樹凹村
****************************************
工作坊形式及階段:
鄉村導賞：認識榕樹凹村落歷史，了解鄉郊地方營造與文化地景。
物資收集：在山海與村落之間收集可用材料。
景觀實踐*：進行場地清理及空間建設實作，由香港建造學院導師帶領鄉村學堂，教授鄉郊景觀實踐技藝與傳統建造方法。
（ * 代表當日將由建造學院導師帶領鄉村學堂及景觀實踐活動。）

月
8日（三）、10日（五）、15日（三） *、16日（四）*
21日（二）、23日（四）、28日（二）、30日（四）

“Reimagining Yung Shue Au: Co-creating a Mountain-Sea Village”
— Recruitment for Rural-placemaking Ambassadors
Re-telling the Yung Shue Au Story: Co-creating Rural Place
The School of Architecture at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently organising a rural school and summer workshop centred on the concept of
rural placemaking
. We invite individuals who are passionate about Hong Kong’s rural culture and interested in hands-on practice to join us in Yung Shue Au and participate in the revitalisation and co-creation of the village landscape.
During the programme, instructors from the Hong Kong Institute of Construction will lead participants in learning traditional construction crafts and rural practical skills. Participants may choose to attend one or multiple workshop sessions according to their availability. Those who complete nine workshop days will receive a service certificate jointly issued by the School of Architecture, CUHK and the Hong Kong Institute of Construction in recognition of their participation and contribution.
Introduction to Yung Shue Au
Located in the northeastern New Territories, Yung Shue Au is a historic Hakka village established over 300 years ago by the Wan clan. At its peak, the village was home to more than 300 residents. Owing to its proximity to the border, a British military camp was stationed in the village during the 1980s, leaving behind a unique yet little-known historical legacy.
Although the village is currently uninhabited, villagers have actively promoted village revitalisation in recent years through repairing ancestral houses, documenting village history, organising village banquets and traditional rituals, as well as reviving the Qilin dance team. These efforts reflect a deep attachment to the village and a strong commitment to cultural inheritance and community reconnection.
Vision
Co-creating Rural Placemaking
Reimagining the mountain-sea landscape through low-carbon restoration and local memories.
Spatial Practice
Improving pathways and communal resting spaces through small-scale construction.

Re-telling the Yung Shue Au Story: Co-creating Rural Place
The School of Architecture at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently organising a rural school and summer workshop centred on the concept of
rural placemaking
. We invite individuals who are passionate about Hong Kong’s rural culture and interested in hands-on practice to join us in Yung Shue Au and participate in the revitalisation and co-creation of the village landscape.
During the programme, instructors from the Hong Kong Institute of Construction will lead participants in learning traditional construction crafts and rural practical skills. Participants may choose to attend one or multiple workshop sessions according to their availability. Those who complete nine workshop days will receive a service certificate jointly issued by the School of Architecture, CUHK and the Hong Kong Institute of Construction in recognition of their participation and contribution.
Introduction to Yung Shue Au
Located in the northeastern New Territories, Yung Shue Au is a historic Hakka village established over 300 years ago by the Wan clan. At its peak, the village was home to more than 300 residents. Owing to its proximity to the border, a British military camp was stationed in the village during the 1980s, leaving behind a unique yet little-known historical legacy.
Although the village is currently uninhabited, villagers have actively promoted village revitalisation in recent years through repairing ancestral houses, documenting village history, organising village banquets and traditional rituals, as well as reviving the Qilin dance team. These efforts reflect a deep attachment to the village and a strong commitment to cultural inheritance and community reconnection.

From: Chu Choi Ying
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mpss@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
The Chinese version follows the English version of this email.
Multicultural Psychological Support Service: Counselling Service for Non-Local Students
No matter where we come from, we all desire to express our emotional needs with no barrier. Speaking in our mother tongue with someone who shares our cultural background not only allows us to better articulate ourselves but also fosters a deeper sense of understanding.
In order to support CUHK non-local students, the Wellness and Counselling Centre (WACC) of the Office of Student Affairs (OSA) offers Multicultural Psychological Support Service. This service allows students to receive counselling services in a comfortable environment.
The service is provided by St John’s Cathedral Counselling Service, and it is available to all CUHK full-time non-local students. The counsellors from St John’s Cathedral Counselling Service are capable of providing counselling services in English or Putonghua, as well as other languages including English, Putonghua, French, German, Dutch, Spanish, Hindi, Indonesian, Japanese, Portuguese, Korean, Urdu, Russian, Sindhi and Tagalog (subject to counsellor’s availability). Below are the specific details of the services provided:
Location:
St John’s Cathedral Counselling Service
Address:
10th Floor, Two Chinachem Plaza, 68 Connaught Road, Central
Website:
https://www.sjccs.hk/
Service Period:
July 2026 to May 2027
Opening hours:
9AM to 9PM Monday to Saturday, except on Public Holiday
Service Target:
All CUHK full-time non-local students, including exchange students.
Local students with extensive exposure to cultural experiences outside Hong Kong are also eligible (e.g. with international school backgrounds, or ethnic minorities born in Hong Kong).
Session:
6 counselling sessions
For more information about the Multicultural Psychological Support Service, please visit
OSA WACC website
or contact WACC staff at 3943 9951 or 3943 7208.
How can I make an appointment?
Enroll online by webform:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13733096
If you have an urgent need to see a counsellor, you may visit WACC during office hours. The Duty Counsellor will assess your needs and make appropriate arrangements with you. If you need emotional support during non-office hours, please call the CUHK 24-hour Emotional Support Hotline at 5400 2055 (exclusively for CUHK Full-time Students and Part-time PGDE Students).
Enquiries:
Contact number: 3943 9951/ 3943 7208
Email:
mpss@cuhk.edu.hk
/
wacc@cuhk.edu.hk
Best regards,
Multicultural Psychological Support Service (MPSS)
Wellness and Counselling Centre
Office of Student Affairs
3/F Pommerenke Student Centre, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shatin, N.T.
T: +852 3943 9951   E:
mpss@cuhk.edu.hk
多元文化心理支援服務
為非本地學生提供母語輔導服務
無論來自哪裡，我們都渴望輕鬆地表達感受。用母語與有相似文化背景的人交談，不僅讓我們能清楚表達自己，還可增強更深層次的理解。為支援非本地同學，學生事務處心理健康及輔導中心推出「多元文化心理支援服務」，讓同學可在舒服自在的情況下打開心扉。

服務提供者：
聖約翰座堂輔導服務中心
服務地址：
中環幹諾道中
68
號華懋廣場Ⅱ期
10
樓
網址：
https://www.sjccs.hk/
服務時段：
2026年7月至2027年5月
營業時間：
週一至週六上午 9 時至晚上 9 時，公眾假期除外
服務對象：
香港中文大學全日制非本地學生，包括交換生
本地學生如有豐富的非本地文化背景（如曾就讀國際學校，或在香港出生的少數族裔人士）亦可申請
輔導次數：
提供6次輔導服務
有關「多元文化心理支援服務」的詳情，請瀏覽
學生事務處心理健康及輔導中心網頁
或致電3943 9951或3943 7208向心理健康及輔導中心職員查詢。
如何預約輔導服務？
於網上預約:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13733096
如急需與輔導員見面，可於辦公時間內到訪位於龐萬倫學生中心2樓的心理健康及輔導中心。當值的輔導員會評估同學的需要，並作出適當的安排。如欲在非辦公時間尋求情緒支援，歡迎致電中大24小時情緒支援熱線5400 2055（僅供中文大學全日制學生及兼讀制學位教師教育文憑學生使用）。
查詢：
致電：3943 9951/3943 7208
電郵：

From: Chen Yang, Xie Chen
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155249610@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
失眠吃安眠藥都沒用？來試試新方法
，
改善失眠，完成
可獲得600超市禮券

初步研究已表明在深度睡眠期間播放特殊處理過的低頻聲波，可改善睡眠品質。本研究用於調查聲音刺激是否可顯著改善失眠症狀，招募符合以下條件的人群參與研究：
18至45歲成年人
無嚴重精神障礙疾病
確診患有失眠症（即出現失眠症狀，每週發作至少三次，持續不少於三個月，並對日間工作、學習或社交造成影響）
能閱讀繁體中文或廣東話
研究流程
:

Investigating a New Intervention for Insomnia. Participants with insomnia are invited — Receive a $600 shopping voucher
Department of Psychiatry
Struggling to fall asleep at night? Feeling distressed by insomnia? Are sleeping medications not helping? We invite you to try a new approach!
Participant recruitment for an insomnia research study is now open.
Acoustic stimulation

We are now recruiting participants who meet the following criteria:
Adults aged
18 to 45
No history of severe psychiatric disorders
Diagnosed with
insomnia disorder
(i.e., experiencing insomnia symptoms at least three times per week for a minimum of three months, with negative impact on daytime work, study, or social functioning)
Able to read Traditional Chinese or Cantonese
Study Procedures
Wear an
actigraphy watch for 14 days
and complete a
sleep diary (7 consecutive days, separately)
On the morning of Day 8, attend the
Sleep Research Laboratory, 7/F Sha Tin Hospital
for a full-day assessment, including:
Cognitive testing
Mood and sleep evaluations
Questionnaire completion
Overnight
polysomnography (sleep study)
Acoustic stimulation may be delivered during deep sleep
Discharge the following morning (
medical leave certificate can be provided

A
personalized sleep report
prepared by experts

$600 supermarket shopping voucher

Announcements
⭐ [CUHK Ophthalmology] Invitation for Thyroid Disease Patients for Free Eye Screening ⭐⭐【中大眼科】招募甲狀腺疾病人士參與免費眼科篩檢 - Department of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences (OVS)
From: Hanson Wong (OVS)
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
⭐⭐
【中大眼科】招募甲狀腺疾病人士參與免費眼科篩檢
【香港中文大學眼科研究】招募甲狀腺疾病人士參與免費眼科篩檢及臨床研究
香港中文大學醫學院眼科及視覺科學學系現正進行一項臨床研究，誠邀已確診或懷疑患有甲狀腺疾病人士參與免費眼科篩檢，以評估是否患有甲狀腺眼病（Thyroid Eye Disease, TED），以及是否適合參與後續臨床研究。
什麼是甲狀腺眼病？
甲狀腺眼病是常見於甲狀腺疾病（如格里夫氏症）的眼部併發症，可引致以下情況：
眼乾、刺痛或流淚
眼皮腫脹或向上收縮
眼球突出（俗稱「眼凸」）
外觀改變，甚至影響視力
及早發現及治療，有助減低病情惡化的風險。
招募對象
符合以下條件人士歡迎參加：
年齡介乎
18
至
80
歲
已確診或懷疑患有甲狀腺疾病（包括甲亢或甲減）
輕至中度甲狀腺眼病患者（已確診或懷疑）
未曾接受甲狀腺眼病相關治療
非懷孕或非哺乳人士
能理解粵語、普通話或英語，並能閱讀中文或英文
即使未確定是否患有甲狀腺眼病，只要曾患甲狀腺疾病，亦歡迎參加篩檢。
研究內容及安排
免費全面眼科檢查
由專業眼科醫生評估及跟進
所有研究相關檢查及評估費用全免
符合資格者將獲邀參與為期約
12
個月
的臨床藥物研究
地點（由研究團隊安排）：
香港中文大學眼科中心（九龍）
或 香港中文大學醫院（沙田）
（最終是否符合研究資格將由研究團隊作進一步評估）
報名及詳情
請透過以下連結登記參與甲狀腺眼病篩檢：

立即登記篩檢
研究團隊將與合資格人士聯絡，安排進一步篩查。
查詢
香港中文大學醫學院眼科及視覺科學學系
電話：3943 0790（何小姐）
WhatsApp：5632 3683
請註明：「查詢 SAVEMORETED 甲狀腺眼疾藥物臨床研究」
您的參與不僅有助及早了解自身眼睛健康狀況，亦有助推動甲狀腺眼病的醫學研究，為未來患者帶來更多治療可能。
The Department of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) is currently conducting a clinical study on Thyroid Eye Disease (TED). We warmly invite individuals with confirmed or suspected thyroid disorders to participate in a
free comprehensive eye screening
to assess for TED and potential eligibility for further clinical research.
What is Thyroid Eye Disease (TED)?
Thyroid Eye Disease is a condition commonly associated with thyroid disorders such as Graves’ disease. It may lead to:
Dryness, irritation, or excessive tearing
Eyelid swelling or retraction
Protrusion of the eyes (proptosis)
Changes in appearance and, in some cases, vision impairment
Early detection and appropriate management are important to reduce the risk of disease progression.
Eligibility Criteria
Individuals who meet the following criteria are welcome to participate:
Aged
18 to 80 years
Diagnosed with or suspected of having thyroid disorders (hyperthyroidism or hypothyroidism)
Diagnosed with or suspected of having
mild to moderate Thyroid Eye Disease
Have
not received prior treatment
specifically for Thyroid Eye Disease
Not pregnant or breastfeeding
Able to understand Cantonese, Mandarin, or English, and read Chinese or English
Individuals who are unsure whether they have Thyroid Eye Disease are also encouraged to join the screening if they have a history of thyroid conditions.
Study Details
Participants will receive:
Free comprehensive ophthalmic examination
Professional assessment and follow-up by ophthalmologists
All study-related examinations at no cost
Eligible participants may be invited to join a
12-month clinical drug study
, subject to further screening and eligibility assessment.

Study locations (by arrangement):
CUHK Eye Centre (Kowloon)
CUHK Medical Centre (Sha Tin)
Registration and Further Information
To register for the Thyroid Eye Disease screening, please visit:

Register for TED Screening
Our research team will contact eligible applicants to arrange further screening.
Enquiries
Department of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences
Faculty of Medicine, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Tel: 3943 0790 (Ms. Ho)
WhatsApp: 5632 3683
Please specify: “SAVEMORETED Clinical Study Enquiry”
Participation in this study not only helps you better understand your eye health, but also contributes to advancing research and improving treatment options for patients with Thyroid Eye Disease.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

香港中文大學手語及聾人研究中心招募研究參與者
香港中文大學手語及聾人研究中心現正進行一項探討中文閱讀模式的研究，誠邀符合以下條件的人士參與：
年齡介乎18至50歲
香港中文大學全日制學生
正常聽力
正常視力或矯正至正常視力
沒有神經、語言或閱讀障礙病史
從未學習過任何手語
此外，參加者須符合以下其中一組條件：
A
組：
香港廣東話母語者
能熟練閱讀及書寫繁體中文
B組：
中國內地普通話母語者
能熟練閱讀及書寫簡體中文
實驗內容及時間
：
A組：參與1個電腦判斷實驗及3個眼動追蹤實驗，共4次實驗，每次約2小時。
B組：參與1個電腦判斷實驗，共1次實驗，約2小時。
地點：
香港中文大學教研樓二座（近科學園）
車馬費：
